item.text: {"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"During the 2023 period, executed administrative and state resources show substantial mobilization toward selected Sisi-era programs, but not demonstrably effective mobilization across the full development portfolio. The presidency reviewed the relocation of more than 100 agencies, including 30 ministries and about 40,000 employees, to the New Administrative Capital; this is direct evidence of presidential coordination, though the official account does not independently verify implementation quality (BATCH-0019-E001). Government commitments to rehabilitate irrigation canals, expand wastewater reuse, and build treatment and desalination facilities were accompanied by military implementation of canals, wells, treatment plants, and the New Delta water system, although completion and outcomes were not established by the end of 2023 (BATCH-0009-R10-E008). The state also mobilized ministries, prosecutors, and interministerial bodies for anti-trafficking work through specialized offices, judicial circuits, strategies, training, and coordination, but these measures were implemented by subordinate institutions and government reports; inconsistent procedures, declining victim identification, inadequate services, and reliance on NGOs and international organizations qualify their effectiveness (BATCH-0008-E007; BATCH-0023-E015). The military's expanded management of civilian projects is attributable to Sisi's delegation strategy and reflects strong centralized resource mobilization, but military reach, arms deliveries, project scale, or administrative activity alone do not establish effective use of resources toward the full portfolio (BATCH-0009-R10-E001; BATCH-0015-E005; BATCH-0011-E008). Major qualifications are weak interagency coordination and implementation mechanisms, absent or unreleased feasibility and environmental studies, opaque military finances and project data, substantial military autonomy, debt-financed and potentially misallocated investment, marginalization of small farmers, and groundwater and resource risks (BATCH-0009-R10-E002; BATCH-0009-R10-E003; BATCH-0009-R10-E009; BATCH-0009-R10-E014; BATCH-0009-R11-E001; BATCH-0009-R11-E006; BATCH-0009-R11-E010). Accordingly, the evidence supports real, concentrated, ruler-attributable mobilization in selected sectors, but only mixed and uncertain effectiveness; WFP operations at Rafah and partner-led activities should not be treated as personal presidential mobilization without evidence of Sisi's direct control (BATCH-0019-E008;
